summary: Iteration_16 re-verification of two HIGH fixes on top of iteration_15. RESULT: FIX-2 (Credit sale end-to-end) is FULLY VERIFIED as working — no error, redirect to /(tabs)/billing succeeds, sale row appears (TB-0013 · Credit Test QA · Apollo Amazer 185/65 R15 · ₹4,484 · Credit), KhataBook now shows a live entry for mobile 9990002222 (OWES ₹8,968 / 2 sales) and Cash regression (TB-0012 · Cash Test QA · Apollo Amazer) also visible → both Credit and Cash paths work. FIX-1 (tyre-form cold-URL race) is PARTIALLY fixed but STILL FAILS on hard-refresh: `page.goto('/inventory/tyre-form')` on a fresh browser tab still redirects to /inventory within ~5s. Root cause: AuthContext.tsx has a failsafe timer at 1500ms that force-flips `initializing → false` even if the Firebase auth persistence layer has NOT yet re-hydrated the user from IndexedDB. usePermissions() maps `loading` to `initializing`, so the tyre-form's `if (perms.loading) return <Loading/>` guard is dismissed at 1500ms, then `!perms.canEditStock` evaluates true (user is still null from Firebase's perspective), and the <Redirect/> fires. Regression-1 items (Owner Admin Panel banner, Admin → Users list with 4 accounts incl. the new qa.owner+1785851063, Inventory tab with New/Old/Remould chip filters) all still PASS. Adding a tyre via the UI's 'Add Tyre' button works correctly (no race) — the deep-link/hard-refresh path is the only remaining failure mode.

ui_bugs.issue: Line 34-36: `setTimeout(() => setInitializing(false), 1500)` is racing the Firebase auth persistence restore (IndexedDB → onAuthStateChanged). On a hard-refresh / cold URL, the 1500ms failsafe fires BEFORE Firebase has restored the user, so `initializing` flips to false while `user` is still null. The `usePermissions().loading` gate in /app/frontend/app/inventory/tyre-form.tsx (line 96) is then satisfied and the `!perms.canEditStock` guard immediately redirects the Owner out. Reference: /app/frontend/src/context/AuthContext.tsx:34, /app/frontend/app/inventory/tyre-form.tsx:96-107

action_items: MAIN AGENT (E1) — HIGH: Extend `usePermissions().loading` semantics OR the AuthContext failsafe. Recommended: change the loading definition so it stays true until EITHER (a) Firebase's onAuthStateChanged has fired with a definitive user (or null) — i.e. wait for the FIRST auth event — OR (b) increase failsafe to ~4000ms and gate `initializing=false` on both `subscribeAuth` having fired at least once AND the timeout. Alternative: in tyre-form.tsx, don't rely solely on `perms.loading`; also check `user === undefined` vs. `user === null` and delay the redirect until we have a confirmed 'no user' signal from Firebase (e.g. auth.currentUser after `onAuthStateChanged` fires at least once). File: /app/frontend/src/context/AuthContext.tsx:34-36 and /app/frontend/src/firebase/auth.ts (subscribeAuth).

critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/context/AuthContext.tsx:33-36 — The 1500ms failsafe is well-intentioned (prevents the splash from hanging if Firebase never fires) but it defeats the `perms.loading` gate that iteration_16 was designed to add. In practice Firebase's IndexedDB restore usually completes in <500ms, but under a cold-navigation deep-link with network latency it can take longer. The failsafe should be raised OR combined with an 'auth has fired at least once' flag.

/app/frontend/app/inventory/tyre-form.tsx:96-107 — The `if (perms.loading) return <Loading/>` fix is CORRECT in concept but insufficient because `perms.loading = initializing` is force-cleared by the AuthContext failsafe. The tyre-form itself needs no further changes once AuthContext exposes a truthful `initializing` value.

/app/frontend/app/sales/new.tsx:164-192 — Post-write side-effects properly wrapped in try/catch. Console warns fire but don't block redirect. The Credit path now works exactly as intended: sale writes first, khata second (with its own try/catch), PDF share third (fire-and-forget with catch). rca_of_issue: FIX-1 RCA: On hard-refresh of /inventory/tyre-form, three async processes are competing: (A) Firebase auth SDK reads persisted session from IndexedDB → fires subscribeAuth callback → setUser(u) + setInitializing(false). Typical latency in Playwright web preview: 800-2500ms. (B) The failsafe `setTimeout(() => setInitializing(false), 1500)` in AuthContext.tsx line 34-36 — fires unconditionally at 1500ms. (C) The tyre-form's `if (perms.loading) return <Loading/>` gate — clears as soon as initializing===false, whichever of (A) or (B) wins. When (B) wins the race (which is very common in web preview with slow network), the loading gate is cleared while `user===null`, `perms.canEditStock===false`, and the `<Redirect href="/(tabs)/inventory" />` on line 107 fires. Reproduction: goto /inventory/tyre-form on any browser tab that was NOT previously on the dashboard → 100% redirect within ~1.6s. Mitigation options for main agent: (1) BEST — track a separate flag `authFired` that is set to true only inside the subscribeAuth callback; expose `loading = !authFired`. Keep the 1500ms failsafe only to set initializing→false so the splash screen still un-hangs, but don't let it satisfy the tyre-form gate. (2) Simpler — bump failsafe to 4000ms and add a `waitForAuth` promise that resolves on first callback fire. (3) In tyre-form.tsx, additionally check `user===undefined` and delay redirect until first auth event.
